title: After the Hardening Run, the App Lost Its Database
symptom: A security hardening script ran on app-1 last night. Since then the app can't reach its PostgreSQL database on db-1. The database is up, and two other app servers that weren't hardened yet connect to it fine. Fix app-1 without undoing the rest of the hardening.

goals.description: app-1's firewall lets it reach PostgreSQL

options: A test rule from the hardening run, left in app-1's OUTPUT chain, dropped outgoing traffic to port 5432 on the local subnet, so connections timed out instead of being refused

debrief: A timeout rather than 'connection refused' means packets are being dropped, not answered: something between app-1 and PostgreSQL silently discards them. Since other servers reach db-1, the place to look was app-1's own firewall, and its OUTPUT chain had a DROP for tcp/5432 to 10.0.1.0/24, commented 'CIS 3.5 test - remove after review'. Deleting that one rule by its line number fixes it without touching anything else. The tempting shortcut, 'iptables -F', would also have wiped the INPUT rules, and with INPUT's policy at DROP that cuts off SSH, including your own session. Firewall changes deserve the same review as code: rules in version control, applied by configuration management, and tested against the connections the host actually needs.
